newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo pleased with early antidepressant sales.
newsitem.headline: Akzo pleased with early antidepressant sales.

text.p: Organon, the pharmaceuticals arm of Dutch group Akzo Nobel, said Friday it was pleased with early sales of its novel antidepressant Remeron.

Remeron, which was rolled out in the Dutch market two years ago, won Food & Drug Administration approval earlier this year and came out in the United States in July. The drug was launched as Remergil in Germany in April 1996.
"We are very happy with early sales," Ron Huisman from Organon's marketing department said at a press briefing on the eve of a European College of Neuropsychopharmacology congress in Amsterdam.

Remeron (mirtazapine) is a novel dual-action compound which acts on both the brain's neurotransmitter systems, where an imbalance is believed to cause depression. Depression is a disease that affects 340 million people worldwide by conservative estimates.
Organon claims its new drug has fewer side-effects than other antidepressants.

Huisman said that monthly sales of the drug in Germany were around one million marks ($661,000) while, after a slow start, Dutch sales were running at around 400,000 to 500,000 guilders ($236,000 to $294,000) a month.
He said Remergil had taken a 2 percent market share in Germany after just two months. He said U.S. sales were on target, but it was too early to analyse.
Sales of the current best-selling treatment for depression, Prozac, manufactured by Indianapolis-based drug company Eli Lilly & Co., were over $2 billion in 1995.
